verdicts.claim: 11 of the 25 `## 3. High-Confidence Synthesis` blocks in ideation-cx.md are hard-truncated mid-word / mid-clause, and the cut content exists nowhere else in the tree.
verdicts.reason: TRUNCATION HALF CONFIRMED EXACTLY. Byte-level measurement of ideation-cx.md: `- **Synthesis**:` lines 350, 356, 362, 368, 380, 386, 392, 398, 404, 422 are each exactly 817 chars and line 374 is 1313, and all 11 end mid-token — L350 tail 'routes around embar', L362 'carries as unatteste', L380 'probable merge. Near-col', L404 'authoritatively lifts embar', L422 'merge retires an identifier — a live'. Every fragment the finding quotes is present verbatim at the cited line (5/5 spot-checks true). Lines 410 (660 chars) and 416 (813) do end on a full stop, exactly as claimed, so the 11-of-25 count is correct and not inflated. All 11 fall in one contiguous run of 02-* pair blocks (02-03 through 02-16), and ideation-cx.md:5 does still declare `**Status**: [DEEP]`. The §1 registry rows (17-41) are NOT truncated (all 25 end with a closing pipe), so the defect is confined to §3. UNRECOVERABILITY HALF REFUTED. The finding tested recoverability by grepping for its own truncated strings, which can only ever hit the source line. Testing for the RULE instead, every pair named in the failure scenario is fully documented in a partner-domain [DEEP] child file: 02-05 (L362) at 05-services-marketplace/05.06-rights-warranties-transfer/05.06.03-rights-transfer-split-execution.md:197 '02 must accept an emitted **claim** at the moment of commit and carry `unattested` / `attested` / `contested` independently' plus DT-06 at :176; 02-12 (L404) at 02-credits-attribution/02.01-credit-graph-discography/02.01.01-credit-record-contribution-ledger.md:184 'The release event authoritatively lifts embargo (`02.01.05` D-03)'; 02-16 (L422 — the finding's headline dead end) at 16-venues-studios-spaces/16.01-place-records-rooms/16.01.01-place-record-type-taxonomy.md:233 'A credit (02) cites a place that has since relocated, renamed, or merged | The citation must resolve to the record **as of the cited date**, not to its current state ... Owned by 02; flagged as Q-06', reinforced by D-04 at :196/:251 and the DT-15 rejection at :284. §3 also self-describes as a digest, not the source of record (ideation-cx.md:272 'Condensed 5-question synthesis ... Full detail lives in the source-domain CX file'), and the intact `- **Interaction**:` line above each truncated block carries the pair's load-bearing constraint. One residual defect is real: the §2 Detail column routes all 22 02-* pairs to 02-credits-attribution/credits-attribution-cx.md (verified L73-L91, L183-L185), and that file holds only intra-domain pairs CX-01..CX-18 plus routed mechanisms and rejected pairs — no domain-pair synthesis — so the named escape hatch is a dead end even though the content exists one level deeper. Net: a real file-integrity defect worth repairing, but no implementer is forced to invent product behaviour, so blocking is not warranted.

verdicts.claim: The `CX-M##` cross-cut identifier space — referenced 830 times across 132 ideation files, including in the root files — is defined in no file, and the two candidate tables give conflicting answers for the same id.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — the conflict is manufactured and the id space resolves unambiguously. Measured: 983 CX-M refs (not 830) across 132 files, 31 distinct ids in use (CX-M26 unused). Exhaustive test: for every one of those 31 ids, at least one occurrence in the tree carries the mechanism name inline, and in all 31 cases that name matches domain-map-proposal.md's `## Cross-cutting systems` row at exactly that ordinal — CX-M01 Payments (:342), CX-M04 Atomic Payment ↔ Rights Transfer (:345), CX-M05 Availability/Scheduling (:346, matching usage '`CX-M05`'s atomic hold serializes it' at 06.01.01:102), CX-M11 Real-Time Rooms (:352), CX-M14 Shipping (:355), CX-M24 Subscriptions & Entitlements (:365), CX-M31 Safeguarding (:372), CX-M32 Offline resilience (:373). Zero id resolves two ways across the tree. The claimed contradiction rests on counting rows in ideation-cx.md §1, but that table's header is `| Mechanism | Owner | Serves | Definition | Key constraints |` (:15) — it has no id column and therefore asserts no id→name binding at all; positional inference over an unnumbered table is the auditor's own construction, not a statement the specs make. The 'CX-M31 has no referent in a 25-row table' argument fails for the same reason, and CX-M31 is in fact name-bound at 06.01.01:196 and gear-marketplace-cx.md:389. 330 of 983 refs carry the name inline, so no id is bare everywhere. Two competent implementers converge on identical referents. The only residual is discoverability — no single legend table publishes the binding — which is a nit, not ambiguity. (Unrelated aside, out of root scope: gear-marketplace-cx.md:382 labels CX-M11 'Messaging & Conversations' while :390 in the same file labels it 'Real-Time Rooms' — a domain-13 typo, not a root-file defect.)

verdicts.claim: Eight of the 32 ratified cross-cutting systems in domain-map-proposal.md have no row in the 25-mechanism registry ideation-cx.md presents as the consolidated one, and no root file records them as merged, renamed, dropped or deferred.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED by full set-difference. domain-map-proposal.md's `## Cross-cutting systems` table (heading :338, rows :342-:373) holds exactly 32 rows; ideation-cx.md §1 (:17-:41) holds exactly 25. Diffing them, §1 absorbs several proposal rows explicitly (Geo :354 and SEO/Embeds :364 folded into 'Search & Discovery' :35, Bulk Import :370 folded into 'Integrations, Public API & Webhooks' :40 whose definition names 'bulk import/sync/migration tooling') and adds three of its own (Split-Capture Trigger, Verified-Credit-as-Evidence, Object & Evidence Storage). The 8 with no row and no absorbing mention are precisely the ones listed: Atomic Payment ↔ Rights Transfer (:345), DAW & Desktop Bridge (:353), Onboarding & Role-Aware Activation (:356), Accessibility (:362), Promoted Placement & Advertising (:366), Referrals, Invites & Affiliates (:367), Follow, Save & Watchlist (:369), Offline & Low-Connectivity Field Resilience (:373). Searched every root and meta file for those 8 names: they appear ONLY in domain-map-proposal.md — zero hits in ideation-cx.md, ideation-index.md, or any of the 6 meta/ files including meta/cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md, and §1b holds only 2 unrelated candidates (Timestamped Annotation, Practice-Room Tools, :49-:50), so they are not tracked as deferrals either. Seven are alive by id (CX-M04 21 refs, CX-M12 2, CX-M15 19, CX-M21 7, CX-M25 10, CX-M28 22, CX-M32 12) and by name in domain files, e.g. 20.05.02:109 'Consumes **CX-M12 DAW & Desktop Bridge**'. The two inventories are counted side by side without reconciliation: ideation-index.md:74 'Cross-cut mechanisms (consolidated registry) | **25** — in `ideation-cx.md`' vs :202 (D-16) '24 domains, 423 candidate sub-domains, 32 cross-cuts'. Warning, not blocking: the proposal row supplies a Purpose and an Affected-domains list, so a consumer is not inventing the mechanism from nothing — what is missing for these 8 is the Owner and Key-constraints columns the registry exists to publish, and the record of where each went.

verdicts.claim: domain-map-proposal.md still carries "DAW & Desktop Bridge" as a ratified cross-cutting system with no marker, while D-70 in the index prohibits any locally-installed client.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — D-70 itself preserves the bridge, so both statements hold. Every quote checks out (proposal:353 verbatim, proposal:440 'Status: [RATIFIED — owner reaffirmed the 24-domain classification on 2026-07-19...]' verbatim, index:143-144 designating the proposal for cross-cuts verbatim, D-70(a) at index:255 verbatim). But reading D-70 to its end refutes the conflict: clause (c) states '`07.09.01/.02/.03` keep **`Should`, unphased**; no ledger change, and the six bridge-dependent features are not re-scoped.' D-70 is therefore not a prohibition on desktop/DAW integration as scope — it is a v1 authorisation gate on shipping a non-web client, with the bridge features deliberately retained in the tree and a named four-item reopening path ('commercial-studio installability (`07.09.01` Q-02 / DT-03(b))', real-session evidence, a costed agent build, a verifiable read-scope model), tracked as vision.md Q-07. A cross-cut row describing the 'Desktop and DAW-host boundary for capture, asset, and workflow integration' serving six domains is exactly consistent with six Should-level unphased features, and the live consumer reference at 20.05.02:109 reads the same way. proposal:440's RATIFIED stamp is also scoped by its own words to 'the 24-domain classification', not to per-cross-cut v1 authorisation, and the proposal's own framing (:7 'a proposal for owner review ... preserves recovered facts') is not a release-scope commitment. No implementer reading D-70 would plan a v1 desktop client; none reading proposal:353 is told to.

verdicts.claim: domain-map-proposal.md lists "band" (and ~40 other role names) under **Personas** for nine domains, contradicting D-19's rule that Band is an entity and not a persona, and the index's zero-invented-personas claim.
verdicts.reason: REFUTED — no reasonable reading builds a Band persona column. The quotes are accurate (proposal:60 'Working musician; band; manager; agent; studio owner; venue operator; label; dealer/shop.', with band/band treasurer also at :84, :144, :240, :252, :264, :288, :324 — 8 lines, not nine domains), and D-19 at index:205 says verbatim 'Band is an **entity** (domain 01), not a persona.' But three things converge against divergence. (1) Authority is designated elsewhere: index:143-144 scopes the proposal to 'Ratified recovery provenance, per-domain rationale, cross-cuts, not-product routing, and demotions' — personas are absent from that list, and index:92 names meta/personas.md as the Personas document while :93 routes non-persona actors to meta/counterparties.md under D-71. (2) The lines are self-evidently a recovered raw actor inventory, not a persona vocabulary: the same 24 lines list 'luthier/tech', 'insurer', 'door staff', 'FOH engineer', 'radio plugger', 'accountant', 'reported user' — nobody derives a Role Matrix column set from that, and the proposal's own preamble (:7) says it 'preserves recovered facts, ratified priorities, novelty labels, and ordering'. (3) The counter-signal is loud and everywhere: index:70 'Invented personas | **0**', index:69 'Role Lens coverage | **734 / 734** feature files (2,936 rows = 4 personas × 734, verified)', and ideation-cx.md:283 restating the entity rule operationally. The forced-invention test fails: the normative vocabulary is stated in three places and contradicted only by an inventory list in a recovery document that no downstream workflow reads for personas.

verdicts.claim: moscow-ledger.md's header asserts the exact half of D-20 that D-31 superseded, with no marker and no reference to D-31 anywhere in the file.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED on both halves. moscow-ledger.md:4 reads verbatim '> **Owner decision (D-20)**: all 195 Must-haves retained; sequencing deferred to `/plan-phase`.' Machine count over all 795 lines: `D-31` 0 hits, `v1.5` 0 hits — so the file states the superseded half and contains no pointer to the decision that superseded it, and it has no release/phase column that would carry the split. The index marks that exact clause dead three separate times: :206 (D-20) '~~v1 beachhead sequencing deferred to `/plan-phase`~~ **— the "defer the beachhead" half is AMENDED by D-31**', :296-297 '**✅ Sequencing RESOLVED by D-31 (2026-07-18).** ... this supersedes the earlier "defer the beachhead" position', and :314-315 'the beachhead is chosen (v1 = the spine); `/plan-phase` sequences the ~45 v1 Musts, then the ~26 v1.5 Musts.' The index also demonstrates the convention this file omits, striking superseded text at :215 (D-29 '~~V1 scope = session spine + all 3 marketplaces~~ **SUPERSEDED by D-31.**'). Held at warning rather than blocking: the ledger is a priority inventory reached from the index (:265), the D-31 correction sits 59 lines above that link in the same reading path, and 'sequencing deferred to /plan-phase' remains half-true since /plan-phase still orders within each release. The defect is a stale unmarked assertion in a root file, fixable in one line, not a state where two builds are equally defensible.

verdicts.claim: The Progress Summary's file census contradicts disk under a heading asserting it was read from disk, and locates moscow-ledger.md one directory above where it actually is.
verdicts.reason: CONFIRMED against disk. ideation-index.md:54 asserts '> All counts read from disk, not from agent self-reports.' and :62 then claims '**1,121** (734 features · 190 indexes · 190 CX · 6 meta · 1 super-index (`ideation-index.md`) · not counted: `../vision.md`, `../feature-ledger.md`, `../moscow-ledger.md` live one level up)'. Actual walk of the tree: 1,122 .md files = 734 features + 189 `*-index.md` (excluding the super-index) + 189 `*-cx.md` (excluding ideation-cx.md) + 6 meta + 4 root docs. So the index tally is off by one on the index count however the supers are apportioned, and the census omits domain-map-proposal.md entirely while never accounting for ideation-cx.md as its own line item. The path claim is straightforwardly wrong: existsSync('.../specs/moscow-ledger.md') is false and the parent directory listing (.gitkeep, README.md, architecture, audits, be, be.md, fe, fe.md, feature-ledger.md, ia, ia.md, ideation, index.md, phases, vision.md) contains no moscow-ledger.md, while '.../specs/ideation/moscow-ledger.md' exists and the same document links './moscow-ledger.md' at :265, :321, :324 and :327. '../vision.md' and '../feature-ledger.md' both resolve, so only the third of the three is misplaced. Warning is the ceiling here: this is metadata, not product behaviour, and nothing downstream builds differently — but the assertion is falsifiable, self-declared as disk-verified, and directly misdirects any coverage or scope step that resolves the ledger by the path this line gives.
